paper_metadata.title: Characterization of microstructure in high strength Mg96Y3Zn1 alloy processed by extrusion and equal channel angular pressing

evidence.quote: The Mg96Y3Zn1 alloy processed by extrusion and equal channel angular pressing (ECAP) was investigated.

The experimental material Mg96Y3Zn1 (in at.%) was prepared by ingot metallurgy. The pure Mg, Zn and Mg-25%Y master alloys were molten in a crucible furnace under a protecting gas (0.3%SF6 and 99.7%CO2).

ECAP was conducted at 623 K using a die with the channel angle ĭ=90° and fillet angle Ȍ=0°. This die configuration imposes an effective strain of approximately one per ECAP pass. The samples were processed by route Bc
The maximum YS of 381.45 MPa and UTS of 438.33 MPa were obtained by 2 passes at 623 K.
After 3 passes, it is dominated by the homogeneous equiaxed grains or sub-grains with an average grain size of 400 nm, as shown in Fig. 3(d).
After 4 passes, there is still a mix of non-recrystallization zone and recrystallization zone.
The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of as-cast alloy indicates that the alloy consists of Į-Mg and X-Mg12ZnY, as shown in Fig. 2.

the micrograph of as-cast Mg96Y3Zn1 is typical dendritic morphology.
The fine lamellar structure can be observed inside grain, as marked by arrow. ... According to the SAED pattern, the lamellar structure is proved to be long period stacking (LPS) structure.

several nano-scale precipitates along grain boundaries are also observed, as shown in Fig. 7. The crystal structure of the precipitates has not been identified yet. Chemical analysis by EDS reveals a significant composition difference between precipitate and matrix. As shown in Fig. 7(b), (c), the chemical compositions in precipitate and matrix are Mg-3.31 at.%Y-0.14 at.%Zn and Mg-1.34 at.%Y, respectively.
After a single pass it is apparent that the microstructure consists of non-recrystallization zone surrounded by the recrystallization zone.
In non-recrystallization zone, however, the numerous deformation bands are developed instead of DRX.

mechanisms.name: crack initiation and propagation in X-phase

evidence.quote: the cracks preferentially occur at the interior of X-phase instead of the interface of X-phase/ Į-Mg during tensile deformation. Owing to the high volume fraction of coarse blocks of X-phase in the Mg96Y3Zn1 alloy, cracks are easier to initiate and propagate at the interior of X-phases during tensile test.
accumulated dislocations at initial grain boundaries during extrusion accelerated the DRX process.
